```{r}
library(tidyverse)

```


```{r}
birthday_sim = function(n) {
  birthdays = sample(1:365, size = n, replace = TRUE)
  n_distinct(birthdays) < n
}
```

```{r}
birthday_results =
  expand_grid(
    group_size = 2:50,
    iter = 1:10000
  ) |>
 mutate(
    shared_birthday = map_lgl(group_size, birthday_sim)
   ) |>
  group_by(group_size) |>
  summarize(
    probability = mean(shared_birthday)
  )

```


```{r}

birthday_results |>
  ggplot(aes(x = group_size, y = probability)) +
  geom_line() 
```
The quick increase in probability is counter-intuitive. The curve increases quickly, with a 50% probability at around 23 people, and 90% at around 40 people

# Problem 2

```{r}

longitudinal_df =
  tibble(
    files = list.files("data/"),
    path = str_c("data/", files)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    data = map(path, read_csv)
  ) |>
  unnest(cols = data) |>
  mutate(
    files = str_replace(files, ".csv", ""),
    arm = str_sub(files, 1, 3)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    week_1:week_8,
    names_to = "week",
    values_to = "outcome",
    names_prefix = "week_"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    week = as.numeric(week)
  ) |>
  select(
    subject = files, arm, week, outcome
  )

```
